mixer_geometry.response: Mixer strips now derive their dimensions from the unobscured viewport and reserve a stable base route row. Failure/success notices and additional send routes no longer resize the faders or move existing pan, Mute and Solo controls. Extra routes contribute to the outer scrolling extent and remain reachable. The actual notice-aware clip remains in force, and ordinary scroll clamping at a range boundary is retained.
mixer_geometry.basis: Participants 1, 3, 4 and 5 independently described missed gestures after visible vertical movement. Their observations and original scores are unchanged.

baseline.observed_changes: The old fader lower edge moved from 693 to 643 points with notices and from 693 to 653 with send creation.
baseline.qualification: That initial log contains four failed tests. Three failed on geometry assertions; the short-window case failed because a transient state had no Dismiss label, and is not counted as an independent baseline geometry reproduction.

validation.route_coverage: The existing mixer-flow tests retain path, destination, offscreen, sound-data and history assertions. Actual mouse scrolling exposes routes that now extend below the stable strips; the assertions were not weakened.
validation.native_review: Both Dark and Light 1440x1000 native previews show unchanged fader lengths and readable, complete output/post-send paths after actual wheel scrolling.

mixer_geometry.remaining_validation: Round8 is a fresh participant evaluation and is still in progress; no score improvement is claimed here.

audio_failure.response: The virtual ALSA/Pulse failure remains unresolved in the participant sessions. A separate CPAL-only program reproduced Xrun followed by the same snd_pcm_avail_delay I/O error (5) when 60 ms callback stalls were injected, without RILL code. This establishes a backend recovery path, not the cause of each participant stall. Default and named selections resolve to the same ALSA PCM. A larger requested buffer was not demonstrated to remedy the failure. No audio product fix or sustained-playback reliability improvement is claimed.
audio_failure.basis: All five reports retain their stream failures. The controlled probe and its raw diagnostics are separate technical evidence.
audio_failure.decision: Retain fatal handling of unknown/BackendError events, explicit Retry/Audio setup and raw diagnostics. Keep the round8 lab configuration unchanged for comparison.
audio_failure.remaining_validation: The actual cause, duration and scheduling of participant stalls were not captured. Platform-specific ALSA/Pulse/CPAL stream-state investigation and physical-device tests are separate work; one 20-second run per probe condition does not estimate reliability.

audio_recovery.response: Preserve the observed transport/meter recovery after Retry or selecting the named output, and the repeated failures. Named and default output select the same PCM; changing selection also recreates the stream, so the selected name is not a demonstrated remedy. Participant5 also observed brief resumed transport after control changes: that sequence remains documented, with no causal explanation or reliability fix claimed. A moving playhead and meters do not establish heard audio or sustained healthy playback.
audio_recovery.decision: Keep visible recovery controls and diagnostics. Do not suppress arbitrary EIO errors or restart a healthy stream based on this evidence.
audio_recovery.remaining_validation: Investigate the actual failure/recovery sequence with stream-state and scheduling evidence before changing error classification or restart behavior.

precise_trim.response: All five final WAVs independently verified as exactly 30.000 seconds. Four reports needed a second small snapped edge correction, which remains recorded friction. Participant3 used the existing Properties 123 duration keypad successfully. Keep snapping, source and Undo semantics and the exact duration route; zoomed-out dragging cannot guarantee a chosen subpixel endpoint in one gesture.
precise_trim.decision: Retain current trim behavior and the existing precise entry route. Do not claim that every one-drag endpoint difficulty was fixed by the mixer or new parameter-keypad work.
precise_trim.validation: Existing trim/duration tests pass within the full workspace suite; saved-output verification is in verification-summary.json.
precise_trim.remaining_validation: Any new drag/snapping redesign requires an independently reproduced incorrect endpoint or explicit interaction study.

loop_scope.response: Participant4 left a 30.134-second playback loop while the arrangement and exported WAV were 30.000 seconds. Playback loop and arrangement are separate editable ranges; trimming a clip should not silently rewrite a deliberately chosen loop. Keep visible range readouts and explicit loop-setting controls.
loop_scope.decision: Preserve independent loop scope. The unchanged loop is not reported as an incorrect export duration.
loop_scope.validation: Existing loop-scope and arrangement-export regressions pass in the full workspace suite.

duplicate_tool.response: The toolbar selects the persistent Duplicate tool and displays Click a clip to duplicate. The clip context-menu Duplicate command performs an immediate copy; Participant2 used both successfully. Preserve the consistent distinction between choosing a tool and executing an action. Repeated one-clip copying and initial tool discovery remain documented friction.
duplicate_tool.decision: Keep the visible gesture instruction and immediate context-menu alternative. Do not change tool selection into an immediate copy or claim that repeated copying now needs fewer clicks.
duplicate_tool.validation: Existing tool-gesture and context-menu regressions pass in the full workspace suite.
duplicate_tool.remaining_validation: Bulk-repeat discovery could be evaluated separately; these sessions do not establish its preferred interaction.

native_dialog.response: The transient black GTK picker, delayed paint, upper-left placement and visual mismatch remain recorded limitations. These native dialogs ran without a window manager, so the captures do not isolate an app defect or establish behavior on a normal desktop. Save/export completion was independently verified.
native_dialog.decision: Retain native pickers and report the limitation. Mixer and numeric-keypad work does not fix dialog rendering or placement.
native_dialog.remaining_validation: Reproduce with a normal window manager and native desktop before deciding whether to change picker integration or styling.

name_key_confusion.response: Participant3 mistook apostrophe for lowercase l, then used Clear and successfully applied little orbit. Preserve draft editing, Clear and explicit Apply. Glyph discrimination remains a usability observation; the successful recovery does not erase it.
name_key_confusion.decision: Retain the working naming keyboard. Do not attribute the typo to a proven key-mapping defect or claim the separate numeric keypad change fixes letter recognition.
name_key_confusion.validation: Existing mouse naming and Apply coverage passes in the full workspace suite.
name_key_confusion.remaining_validation: Any glyph or keyboard-layout redesign needs native visual validation of the specific ambiguity.

pan_diagonal.response: Participant4 corrected a diagonal pan gesture with a horizontal drag and used the displayed value to recover. Record that direction-expectation mismatch. The independent final-release bug was demonstrated in input tests; no participant-specific event trace connects it to this diagonal gesture.
pan_diagonal.decision: Preserve the documented relative pan interaction and visible value feedback. Do not attribute this participant reservation or a score improvement to the release fix.
pan_diagonal.validation: Horizontal/vertical, precision, pointer ownership and final-release tests pass in the current shared UI and app suites.
pan_diagonal.remaining_validation: A change to diagonal gesture interpretation would need a separate expectation study or reproducible incorrect behavior.

sparse_mixer_space.response: Participant3 found unused space with three channels. Keep readable channel widths and room for additional channels; adding unrelated panels or stretching a few strips across the entire workspace would undermine the focused mixer and consistent control scale.
sparse_mixer_space.decision: Retain the focused layout and record the appearance preference.
sparse_mixer_space.validation: Compact-window geometry regressions and Dark/Light native previews passed; this is not a newly added feature.

export_wait.response: WAV export visibly took longer than editing or MIDI export and exposed elapsed progress and completion receipts. Preserve asynchronous export and the clear completion record. The simulations include software rendering, tool and screenshot overhead and are not throughput benchmarks.
export_wait.decision: Retain existing progress and completion feedback. No faster export or new completion-time estimate is claimed.
export_wait.validation: Existing asynchronous export, progress and receipt coverage passes in the full workspace suite; saved exports were independently verified.
export_wait.remaining_validation: Throughput optimization requires a controlled export benchmark with an identified bottleneck.

untested_scope.response: The participants found the requested audio/MIDI/VST composition, mixer, save and export features. They did not evaluate effects, recording, automation, other plug-ins or physical hardware. Keep these areas explicitly untested by this study, even where engineering tests exist.
untested_scope.decision: Do not treat unvisited features as absent or turn task completion into full compatibility, audio-quality or completeness assurance.
untested_scope.remaining_validation: A broader claim requires task-specific user sessions and appropriate plug-in/hardware coverage.

positive.response: Preserve the successful workflow identified by the original observation and its screenshots. Independent verification confirms exact 30-second output, saved project/MIDI structure and actual audio/VST contributions. These results do not establish audible musical quality, physical-device behavior or untested feature compatibility.
positive.decision: Keep the working paths and original scores; do not relabel observed pre-existing behavior as a new implementation.
positive.validation: The full current workspace suite passes. A separate fresh round8 evaluation checks the user task after the changes.

send_routing_steps.response: Participant2 noted that adding a send opens Routing and requires another menu. All five participants nevertheless created the requested send. Retain the explicit destination choice and focused routing panel, where send level and pre/post mode remain together; the mixer keeps adjacent Add bus/Add send toolbar entry points and per-strip send controls.
send_routing_steps.decision: Acknowledge the extra steps without claiming they were removed. Keep detailed routing on demand rather than adding permanent per-destination controls to every strip.
send_routing_steps.validation: Existing adjacent-toolbar, send creation and route-reachability E2Es pass, and both-theme native route previews are readable.
send_routing_steps.remaining_validation: A shorter send-creation flow is a future design option, not a demonstrated fix from this iteration.

rating_reservations.reason: Visible double-click-for-MIDI guidance, the instrument assignment button, note generator, and labeled mixer controls let me complete the requested mouse workflow. Duplicate behaved as a tool instead of an immediate command, and exact trimming took a second drag.
The dark teal arranger, visible note previews, colored bus, and routing lines made the project feel coherent and polished. The native file picker looked visually separate.

Generating 56 notes and duplicating audio took few actions, and MIDI export returned quickly. Initial playback errors and retry attempts slowed the session; WAV export displayed a running elapsed counter before success. This rating is subjective and includes laboratory conditions.

Most main labels were clear. Duplicate required clicking a clip after choosing the tool. Reappearing audio-error banners moved the mixer controls vertically, causing missed solo clicks. System default output failed until I selected the named lab output.

I found audio and MIDI arrangement, a VST3 instrument, note generation, volume/pan/mute/solo, a bus and send, a mouse naming keyboard, project save, and both exports. I did not test effects, recording, automation, or other plug-ins.
Visible double-click guidance led directly to the instrument library; Pencil, Duplicate, Mixer, and export labels were usable without keyboard input. Exact trimming needed a small correction.
The dark interface, colored waveforms, clear notes, channel strips, and routing lines looked coherent and polished. Native save dialogs looked visually separate.

Most clicks and drags produced immediate visible changes; repeated MIDI clips were quick to create. Playback needed one retry and native dialogs sometimes appeared after an extra screenshot. WAV export showed elapsed progress and completed.
Low overall confusion because tools describe their actions. Initial playback failure and the very small trim adjustment were the main interruptions; a send required a routing panel and another menu.
rating_reservations.additional_response: A send required Routing and destination selection. All five discovered and completed it; explicit source/destination selection is retained to avoid ambiguous routing. No reduction in steps is claimed.

rating_reservations.reason: This task exposed audio clips, MIDI editing, a VST3 instrument, volume, pan, mute, solo, bus/send routing, naming, save, and two export formats. I did not explore effects or more advanced composition features.

The MIDI hint, note Pencil, numerical property keypad, Mixer labels and export menus let me finish using the mouse. Repeating a one-bar melody needed many clicks and playback recovery interrupted the flow.
The dark interface, teal waveforms, clear piano notes and visible routing lines look coherent and attractive. The Mixer has a lot of unused space with only three channels.

Drawing, duplication, numeric edits and mix controls visibly responded quickly. WAV rendering took roughly tens of seconds and playback needed retries; elapsed session time includes tool and screenshot overhead.

Duplicate is a tool that requires clicking a clip after selecting it. Mixer controls moved vertically when a status banner appeared or disappeared, making follow-up clicks uncertain. I also misread a key on the on-screen keyboard and corrected the name.

I found all requested task features: audio, MIDI notes, the installed VST3, volume/pan/mute/solo, bus/send, project save, WAV and MIDI export. Playback was unreliable in this laboratory session, and broader plugins or advanced production features were not tested.

Visible MIDI hint, Pencil drags, Duplicate instructions, mixer labels and the on-screen naming keyboard enabled all requested editing and file operations. Exact trimming and shifting controls needed correction.
The dark interface, turquoise waveform and note clips, and large mixer strips looked coherent and readable.
Most editing actions responded promptly. WAV export visibly took several seconds and playback repeatedly stopped with an output-stream error, interrupting the task. This is not a benchmark.
Most actions had clear labels. Pan drag direction needed adjustment, precise clip-end snapping was fiddly, and the error banner moved mixer controls underneath subsequent intended clicks.
Found audio and MIDI editing, VST assignment, volume, pan, mute, solo, bus, send, mouse-only naming, save and both exports. Reliable playback was not established in this session.

The empty-lane instruction, instrument assignment, duplication and on-screen keyboard made composition possible with only the mouse. Exact trimming needed a second adjustment, and Mixer controls moved vertically when banners or sends appeared.
The dark interface, teal waveform and note clips, and colored routing arrows looked cohesive and made the finished arrangement easy to scan.
Most edits visibly responded promptly. WAV export showed an elapsed-time indicator; playback required a retry and failed again. This is an interaction impression, not a hardware benchmark.

Duplicate first selected a tool rather than immediately copying; its instruction resolved this. Mixer layout shifts made several attempted pan or solo clicks miss. Playback could briefly resume after a control change despite the preceding failure notice.

Audio, MIDI note drawing, a real installed VST3 assignment, bus/send routing, title entry, project save and both exports were discoverable. Reliable playback was not established in this laboratory session.

status_definitions.implemented_and_validated: A product change is implemented and checked by focused regressions, full workspace validation and native review; a fresh participant result is still separate.
status_definitions.investigated_but_unresolved: Technical evidence narrows the issue without establishing the participant cause or a product remedy.
status_definitions.retained_design_with_reasoned_response: The observation is acknowledged and the current design is deliberately retained for the stated reason; no newly fixed behavior is claimed.
status_definitions.documented_observation_no_causal_fix: The observation and recovery remain in the record, without a demonstrated defect cause or claimed remedy.
status_definitions.coverage_limit: The task did not evaluate the feature or environment; this is neither evidence of absence nor compatibility assurance.
status_definitions.preserve_observed_success: Keep behavior that worked in the observed task; this is not a newly implemented feature.
